mainTopic: Praise of פלטי בן ליש; the mourning king in the משנה; why אבנר was punished; what a דרגש is
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ranking of three men who held back from sin: יוסף, בועז, and פלטי בן ליש, with פלטי at the top. רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן read פסוקים from משלי 31 as hints to this ranking. Two more readings of 'Grace is deceitful, beauty is vain' apply it to generations instead. One of them ends with the generation of רבי יהודה בר אילעאי, whose poor students shared one cloak and still learned תורה. Then a new משנה teaches that a mourning king does not leave his palace. רבי יהודה says he may follow the bier, as דוד did for אבנר, and the חכמים answer that דוד only did it to calm the people. The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same argument about where women walk at a funeral. It then discusses why אבנר was punished: either he failed to protest to שאול, or he delayed דוד's kingdom. Finally, the גמרא asks what a דרגש is. עולא's 'bed of fortune' is rejected, רבין says it is a leather bed, and רבי יוחנן's explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בועז's strength looks small next to פלטי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its ranking: even בועז's great self-control is only a modest level compared to פלטי בן ליש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The strength of בועז was only the humility of פלטי בן ליש, as we said earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a chain that started earlier. The previous link compared יוסף to בועז, and now it says בועז's strength is small compared to פלטי בן ליש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each man's self-control is measured against the next one. בועז held back for one night, but פלטי held back for many nights, so פלטי ranks highest. The words 'as we said' point back to that earlier explanation instead of repeating it.

keyTerms.meaning: His strength, his great power of self-control
His humility or modesty. Here it means something that looks small and modest by comparison
As we said, pointing back to an earlier explanation

phrases.english: The strength of Boaz
is the humility of Palti son of Laish,
as we said.
phrases.notes: בועז held back for one night, but פלטי held back for many nights, as the גמרא explained earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹקְפּוֹ שֶׁל בּוֹעַז עִנְוְותָנוּתוֹ שֶׁל פַּלְטִי בֶּן לַיִשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison chain from before this section (יוסף to בועז, then בועז to פלטי).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פלטי בן ליש's self-control was greater than בועז's, and בועז's was greater than יוסף's.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן reads 'you excel above them all' as פלטי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads משלי 31:29 as hinting to the ranking: יוסף and בועז did valiantly, but פלטי בן ליש excelled above them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: What does the פסוק 'Many daughters have done valiantly, but you excel above them all' mean? 'Many daughters have done valiantly' refers to יוסף and בועז. 'But you excel above them all' refers to פלטי בן ליש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finds a פסוק that matches the ranking the גמרא just made. The first half of the פסוק praises יוסף and בועז, and the second half crowns פלטי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two levels: many did well, and one did better than all of them. רבי יוחנן fits the three men onto those two levels, so יוסף and בועז are good and פלטי is the best. This supports the ranking from step 1 with a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? This is a standard opening for explaining a פסוק
You rose above all of them

steps.whatToRemember: The phrase 'you excel above them all' is read as פלטי בן ליש, who outdid both יוסף and בועז.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Many daughters have done valiantly,
but you excel above them all"?
"Many daughters have done valiantly":
this is Yosef and Boaz.
"But you excel above them all":
this is Palti son of Laish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק that fits the ranking stated in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משלי 31:29 hints that פלטי בן ליש surpassed יוסף and בועז.

steps.title: Grace and beauty versus fear of ה׳: יוסף, בועז, פלטי
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמן, quoting רבי יונתן, reads משלי 31:30 the same way: 'grace' is יוסף, 'beauty' is בועז, and 'fear of ה'' is פלטי בן ליש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמן said in the name of רבי יונתן: What does 'Grace is deceitful and beauty is vain' mean? 'Grace is deceitful' refers to יוסף. 'Beauty is vain' refers to בועז. 'She who fears ה' shall be praised' refers to פלטי בן ליש.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא uses the very next פסוק in משלי to make the same point. The first two praises point to יוסף and בועז, and the highest praise, fear of ה', points to פלטי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling יוסף 'deceitful' and בועז 'vain' is not an insult. It means their goodness looks small next to פלטי's. The פסוק ends by praising fear of ה' above everything else, and that top level is given to פלטי.

keyTerms.meaning: Grace is deceitful, meaning charm is not the real thing
Beauty is vain, meaning beauty is fleeting
She who fears ה' shall be praised

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'deceitful' and 'vain' as criticism of יוסף and בועז. It only means their level looks small compared to פלטי בן ליש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Grace is deceitful, and beauty is vain"?
phrases.notes: משלי 31:30. The פסוק goes on: 'a woman who fears ה', she shall be praised,' and the גמרא uses that part next.

phrases.english: "Grace is deceitful": this is Yosef;
"and beauty is vain": this is Boaz.
"She who fears the Lord shall be praised":
this is Palti son of Laish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel reading of the next פסוק in משלי, supporting the same ranking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משלי 31:30 ranks יוסף and בועז below פלטי בן ליש, whose fear of ה' earns the highest praise.

steps.title: Second reading: the generations of משה, יהושע, and חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: A second reading applies the same פסוק to three generations: the generation of משה, the generation of יהושע, and the generation of חזקיה, which is praised most.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'Grace is deceitful' refers to the generation of משה. 'Beauty is vain' refers to the generation of יהושע. 'She who fears ה' shall be praised' refers to the generation of חזקיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different way to read the same פסוק. Instead of three men, it ranks three generations, with the generation of חזקיה at the top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern of the פסוק stays the same: two good levels, then one level that is praised above them. The גמרא doesn't say here what is being compared. The usual explanation is Torah learning, which flourished in חזקיה's time even under hard conditions. This is a separate reading and does not cancel the earlier one.
steps.whatToRemember: The same פסוק, 'Grace is deceitful, beauty is vain, fear of ה' shall be praised,' can be read about people (יוסף, בועז, פלטי) or about generations (משה, יהושע, חזקיה). Either way, the last level is praised above the first two.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
"Grace is deceitful": this is the generation of Moshe;
"and beauty is vain": this is the generation of Yehoshua;
"She who fears the Lord shall be praised":
this is the generation of Chizkiyahu.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר שֶׁקֶר הַחֵן זֶה דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of the same פסוק from step 3, applying it to generations instead of individuals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משלי 31:30 can also be read as ranking the generation of חזקיה above the generations of משה and יהושע.

steps.title: A third reading: the generation of רבי יהודה בר אילעאי is praised most
steps.stepSummary: Another reading of משלי 31:30. 'Grace' is the generation of משה and יהושע, 'beauty' is the generation of חזקיה, and 'fear of ה'' is the generation of רבי יהודה בר אילעאי, whose six students shared one cloak and still learned תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'Grace is false' is the generation of משה and יהושע. 'Beauty is empty' is the generation of חזקיה. 'Fear of ה' is what is praised' is the generation of רבי יהודה בר אילעאי. They said about him that six of his students would cover themselves with one cloak and still learn תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more way to read the same פסוק about three generations. This time the top level goes to the generation of רבי יהודה בר אילעאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compared with Step 4, the generations of משה and יהושע are now grouped together as 'grace', and חזקיה's generation moves down to 'beauty'. The top spot goes to a later, very poor generation. The proof is that six students shared one cloak and kept learning, so learning תורה through hardship is praised above learning in good times.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation; a new way to read the same פסוק
רבי יהודה son of רבי אילעאי, a תנא

steps.whatToRemember: This closes the אגדה on משלי 31:30. In every reading, the 'fear of ה'' level is the one that stands out as praised most.

phrases.english: Another explanation:

phrases.aramaic: ״שֶׁקֶר הַחֵן״ – זֶה דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: "Grace is false" – this is the generation of Moshe and Yehoshua.
phrases.notes: משלי 31:30, the same פסוק as the step before.

phrases.english: "And beauty is empty" – this is the generation of Chizkiyah.
"Fear of ה׳, she shall be praised" –

phrases.aramaic: זֶה דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִילְעַאי.
phrases.english: this is the generation of Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Ilai.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִילְעַאי,
phrases.english: They said about him, about Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Ilai,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ שִׁשָּׁה תַּלְמִידִים מִתְכַּסִּין בְּטַלִּית אַחַת
phrases.english: that six students would cover themselves with one cloak
and still be busy learning Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different reading of the same פסוק used in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Fear of ה'' in משלי 31:30 is the generation of רבי יהודה בר אילעאי, who learned תורה in deep poverty.

steps.title: New משנה: a king does not leave his palace for a funeral
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that when a relative of the king dies, the king does not go out of his palace door.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a relative of the king dies, the king does not go out of the door of his palace.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a king stays inside his palace when a relative dies and does not go out to escort the dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the משנה's laws about a king's special honor. Leaving the palace to walk after a funeral bier is treated as below the king's dignity.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If a relative of his dies –
phrases.notes: 'His' means the king. This משנה is listing the laws of a king.

phrases.english: he does not go out of the entrance of his palace.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מֵת לוֹ מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and opens a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king does not leave his palace to escort a dead relative.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the king may follow the bier, as דוד did for אבנר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees. If the king wants, he may follow the bier, and he proves it from דוד, who walked after אבנר's bier.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If he wants to go out after the bier, he may, because we find that דוד went after אבנר's bier, as it says: 'And King דוד walked after the bier.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues with the first opinion and lets the king follow the bier if he wishes. He brings a פסוק about דוד as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof is simple. דוד was a king, and the פסוק says he walked after the bier, so a king may do it. He does not require it; it is the king's choice.

keyTerms.meaning: The bier the dead person is carried on
For so we find; brings an example from the past as proof
אבנר בן נר, שאול's general, who was killed by יואב

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם רוֹצֶה לָצֵאת אַחַר הַמִּיטָּה – יוֹצֵא,
phrases.english: if he wants to go out after the bier – he goes out,
for so we find with David,
who went out after the bier of Avner,
as it says: "And King David walked after the bier."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם רוֹצֶה לָצֵאת אַחַר הַמִּיטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: A king may follow a funeral bier if he wants.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 3:31: דוד walked after אבנר's bier.

steps.title: The חכמים: דוד only did it to calm the people
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה's proof. דוד's case was special: he walked after the bier only to calm the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: That was only done to calm the people.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's proof from דוד. They say his case was a one-time exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים accept that דוד walked after the bier, but they deny that it shows the normal rule. דוד needed to show the people he had no part in אבנר's death, so his case cannot teach that every king may do this.

keyTerms.meaning: To calm the people and win them over

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים do not argue with the facts of the פסוק. They agree דוד walked after the bier; they only say it was a special situation.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה הַדָּבָר אֶלָּא לְפַיֵּיס אֶת הָעָם.
phrases.english: the matter was only to calm the people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא הָיָה הַדָּבָר אֶלָּא לְפַיֵּיס אֶת הָעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from דוד, not the story itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: דוד's case was an exception made to calm the people, so it cannot set a general rule for kings.

steps.title: At the comforting meal, the king sits on a special couch
steps.stepSummary: When the people give the king the mourner's meal, everyone sits on the ground, but the king sits on a couch called a דרגש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when they give him the mourner's meal, all the people sit on the ground, and he sits on the couch.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more rule about a king who is mourning. Even as a mourner, he keeps a special honor at the comforting meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally mourners sit low. The king still keeps a mark of royal honor: the people sit on the ground while he sits on a דרגש.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving the mourner his first meal after the burial
A special couch or low bed

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה shows that a king keeps his honor even while mourning: he stays in his palace (or, according to רבי יהודה, may follow the bier), and he sits on a דרגש at the comforting meal.

phrases.english: And when they give him the mourner's meal –
all the people recline on the ground,
and he reclines on the dargash.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁמַּבְרִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's laws about a mourning king.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the mourner's meal, the people sit on the ground and the king sits on a דרגש.

steps.title: ברייתא: women walk where local custom puts them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. Where women are used to walking after the bier, they walk after it, and where they are used to walking in front of it, they walk in front.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: In a place where women are used to going out after the bier, they go after it. Where they are used to going in front of the bier, they go in front.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא about where women walk at a funeral. This sets up רבי יהודה's view in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion leaves it up to local custom. The ברייתא connects to the משנה because רבי יהודה will use the same דוד proof again.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught; introduces a ברייתא
A place where they were used to; local custom

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
a place where women were used
to go out after the bier – they go out after it,
in front of the bier – they go out in front.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with a related מחלוקת that uses the same proof from דוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where women walk at a funeral depends on local custom.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: women always walk in front, as the דוד story shows
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says women always walk in front of the bier. His proof is that דוד walked after אבנר's bier, and he would not have walked among the women.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Women always go in front of the bier, because we find that דוד went after אבנר's bier, as it says: 'And King דוד walked after the bier.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the custom-based rule. He brings the same פסוק about דוד to prove that women always walk in front.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is that men walk behind the bier, as דוד did. A king would not walk among the women, so the women must have been in front. This shows the set order is women in front and men behind.

keyTerms.meaning: Always; in every place, no matter the custom

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
women always go out in front of the bier,
for so we find with David,
who went out after the bier of Avner,
phrases.notes: The point is that דוד was behind with the men, so the women must have been up front.

phrases.english: as it says: "And King David walked after the bier."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם נָשִׁים לִפְנֵי הַמִּיטָּה יוֹצְאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Women always walk in front of the bier.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 3:31: דוד walked after the bier, so he was with the men behind it.

steps.title: The חכמים: דוד moved between men and women to calm everyone
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that דוד was calming the people, and it worked. He kept moving between the men and the women, so his position proves nothing about where women walk.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: That was only done to calm the people, and they were calmed. דוד would leave the men and go among the women, then leave the women and go among the men, as it says: 'All the people and all ישראל knew that the killing of אבנר did not come from the king.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה's proof. They explain that דוד did not stay in one place behind the bier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's proof assumed דוד stayed with the men behind the women. The חכמים say דוד moved back and forth between both groups so that everyone would see he was mourning. So his place in the procession says nothing about the normal order, and they support this with שמואל ב 3:37.

keyTerms.meaning: And they were calmed; the people accepted it

steps.whatToRemember: Both times רבי יהודה uses דוד walking after אבנר's bier, the חכמים answer the same way: דוד's case was special, done to calm the people. So it cannot set a general rule.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה הַדָּבָר אֶלָּא לְפַיֵּיס אֶת הָעָם, וְנִתְפַּיְּיסוּ.
phrases.english: the matter was only to calm the people, and they were calmed.
For David would go out from among the men
and go in among the women,
and go out from among the women
and go in among the men,
as it says: "And all the people and all Israel knew

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֹא הָיְתָה מֵהַמֶּלֶךְ לְהָמִית אֶת אַבְנֵר״.
phrases.english: that it was not from the king to kill Avner."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא הָיָה הַדָּבָר אֶלָּא לְפַיֵּיס אֶת הָעָם, וְנִתְפַּיְּיסוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's proof from Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from דוד's place in the procession.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: דוד moved between the men and the women to calm everyone, so where he walked does not show where women normally walk.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the answer in the משנה (Step 8): 'to calm the people' meant דוד made sure every group saw him mourning אבנר.

steps.title: At first the people wanted to destroy דוד, then they comforted him
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the פסוק about the people coming to comfort דוד is written as 'to destroy' but read as 'to comfort,' showing how their attitude changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא explained: What does the פסוק mean when it says, 'And all the people came to comfort דוד'? It is written 'to destroy' but we read it 'to comfort.' At first they came to destroy him, and in the end they came to comfort him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains a פסוק from אבנר's funeral that is spelled one way and read another way. He uses both versions to tell the story of how the people's feelings toward דוד changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The written word לְהַכְרוֹת (to destroy) and the read word לְהַבְרוֹת (to comfort) differ by just one letter. רבא says both are true: at first the people suspected דוד of killing אבנר and wanted to destroy him. Once they saw he was really mourning, they came to comfort him. This fits step 12, where דוד's efforts to calm the people worked.

keyTerms.meaning: Explained a פסוק to bring out a deeper lesson
It is written (how the word is spelled)
And we read it (how the word is pronounced)
To comfort, to give the mourner's meal

phrases.english: Rava expounded: What is the meaning of that which is written:
"And all the people came to comfort David"?
It is written "to destroy,"
phrases.notes: In the spelling of the פסוק, the word has a כ instead of a ב.

phrases.english: and we read it "to comfort."
At first, they came to destroy him,
and in the end, to comfort him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 12, where דוד calmed the people. It shows from the פסוק that his effort worked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people at first wanted to destroy דוד, but in the end they comforted him.

steps.title: רב says אבנר was punished for not protesting to שאול
steps.stepSummary: רב asks why אבנר was punished with death, and answers that he should have protested to שאול but did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Why was אבנר punished? Because he should have protested to שאול, and he did not protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: why did אבנר deserve to be killed? רב gives his answer: אבנר failed to protest against שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבנר was שאול's army general, so he had the power to speak up. רב holds him responsible for staying quiet. The text does not say what he should have protested, but the classic explanation is שאול's killing of the כהנים of the city נוב.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
For what reason was Abner punished?
Because he should have protested to Saul
and he did not protest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מִפְּנֵי מָה נֶעֱנַשׁ אַבְנֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of אבנר's funeral to a new question about why אבנר died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבנר was punished because he could have protested to שאול and did not.

steps.title: רבי יצחק says אבנר did protest, but no one listened
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק disagrees with רב: אבנר did protest to שאול, but שאול did not listen to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: He did protest, but he was not listened to.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק argues with רב. According to him, אבנר did the right thing and protested. שאול just did not listen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes away רב's reason for the punishment. If אבנר protested, he did his job, so the reason for his death must be something else. The גמרא will come back to this question in step 19.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
He protested, but he was not listened to.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר: מִיחָה וְלֹא נַעֲנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רב's opinion in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבנר protested to שאול, but שאול did not listen.

steps.title: Both opinions come from the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that רב and רבי יצחק both learned their opinions from one פסוק: דוד's lament over אבנר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them learned from the same פסוק: 'And the king lamented for אבנר and said: Should אבנר die as a fool dies? Your hands were not tied, and your feet were not put in chains.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that both opinions come from the same פסוק. This sets up the next two steps, where the גמרא explains how each one reads it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the פסוק is only quoted, not explained. The key words are 'your hands were not tied.' Each opinion will read these words in a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: And he lamented, gave a mourning speech

phrases.english: And both of them expounded one פסוק:
"And the king lamented for Abner, and said:
Should Abner die as a fool dies?
Your hands were not tied,
and your feet were not put into chains."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁנֵיהֶן מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the shared source for the two opinions in steps 14 and 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both opinions about אבנר come from דוד's lament in שמואל ב 3:33–34.

steps.title: How רב reads the פסוק: you were free, so why didn't you protest?
steps.stepSummary: According to the opinion that אבנר did not protest, דוד is blaming him: you were free to protest, so why didn't you? That is why you fell.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says he did not protest explains it this way: 'Your hands were not tied, and your feet were not put in chains.' So why didn't you protest? That is why 'as a man falls before wicked people, you fell.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רב reads the פסוק. דוד is telling אבנר that nothing was stopping him, so his silence was his own fault.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, 'your hands were not tied' means 'you were free to speak up.' Since he could have protested and did not, he died at the hands of wicked people as a punishment.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר לָא מִיחָה, הָכִי קָאָמַר:
phrases.english: The one who says he did not protest explains it this way:
"Your hands were not tied,
and your feet were not put into chains,"
so why didn't you protest?
Therefore, "as a man falls before wicked people, so you fell."
phrases.notes: This is the next part of the same פסוק (3:34).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר לָא מִיחָה, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק from step 16 according to רב in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's words blame אבנר: he was free to protest and didn't, so he fell.

steps.title: How רבי יצחק reads the פסוק: you protested, so why did you fall?
steps.stepSummary: According to the opinion that אבנר did protest, דוד is wondering out loud: you were not held back and you did protest, so why did you die like this?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says he protested but was not listened to reads it as a question of wonder: 'Should אבנר die like a fool? Your hands were not tied, and your feet were not in chains.' Since you did protest, why did you 'fall as a man falls before wicked people'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יצחק reads the same פסוק. Here דוד is not blaming אבנר. He is amazed that a man who did the right thing died this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, 'your hands were not tied' means 'you used your freedom and protested.' So the end of the פסוק, 'so you fell,' becomes a sad question: why did this happen to you? The same words now praise אבנר instead of blaming him.

keyTerms.meaning: He is asking in wonder, in amazement

steps.confusionAlert: The words of the פסוק are exactly the same as in step 17. Only the tone changes: in step 17 it is blame, and here it is a question of wonder.

phrases.english: And the one who says he protested but was not listened to
reads it as a question of wonder:
"Should he die as a fool dies?"
"Your hands were not tied, and your feet were not in chains,"
since you certainly did protest,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא ״כִּנְפוֹל לִפְנֵי בְנֵי עַוְלָה נָפָלְתָּ״?
phrases.english: why then "as a man falls before wicked people, so you fell"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר מִיחָה וְלֹא נַעֲנָה, אַתְמוֹהֵי מַתְמַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יצחק's reading of the same פסוק, the opposite of step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's words express wonder: אבנר protested, so why did he die like this?

steps.title: If אבנר protested, why was he punished?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רבי יצחק, who says אבנר did protest, what was the reason for his punishment?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says he protested, why was he punished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question on רבי יצחק's view. If אבנר did the right thing, there must be some other reason he was killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's opinion already gives a reason for the punishment: not protesting. רבי יצחק took that reason away, so his opinion leaves a gap. The גמרא now asks to fill it.

phrases.english: According to the one who says he protested,
what is the reason he was punished?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִיחָה, מַאי טַעְמָא אִיעֲנַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what follows from רבי יצחק's reading in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A reason for אבנר's death that fits the view that he did protest to שאול.

steps.title: אבנר delayed דוד's kingdom by two and a half years
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רבי יצחק answers that אבנר was punished because he held back the kingdom of דוד for two and a half years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רבי יצחק said: Because he delayed the kingdom of the house of דוד for two and a half years.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר רבי יצחק answers the question from step 19. אבנר was punished for keeping דוד from becoming king over all of ישראל sooner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After שאול died, אבנר supported שאול's son איש בשת as king instead of דוד. That delayed דוד's rule by two and a half years. So even according to רבי יצחק, there is a clear reason for אבנר's punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: The kingdom of the house of דוד

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons given for אבנר's death. According to רב, he did not protest to שאול. According to רבי יצחק, he did protest, but he was punished for delaying דוד's kingdom by two and a half years.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman, son of Rabbi Yitzchak, said:
Because he delayed the kingdom of the house of David
for two and a half years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק: שֶׁשִּׁהָא מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אבנר was punished for delaying דוד's kingdom by two and a half years.

steps.title: What is a דרגש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about comforting the mourning king and asks what a דרגש is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And when they comfort him,' and so on, mentioning that the king reclines on a דרגש. What is a דרגש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה and asks what the word דרגש means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that when the king is given his meal of comfort, he reclines on a דרגש. The word is unfamiliar, so the גמרא wants a definition before going further.

keyTerms.meaning: And when they give the meal of comfort, the first meal friends serve a mourner
A type of couch or bed mentioned in the משנה
'Etc.', meaning the rest of the quote from the משנה

phrases.english: And when they comfort him, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: when the mourning king gets his meal of comfort, everyone sits on the floor and he reclines on a דרגש.

phrases.english: What is a dargash?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דַּרְגֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of אבנר and returns to explaining a word in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word דרגש in the משנה.

steps.title: עולא: a bed of fortune
steps.stepSummary: עולא defines a דרגש as a 'bed of fortune.'
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: it is a bed of fortune.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers that a דרגש is an ערסא דגדא, a 'bed of fortune.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In those days people kept a special bed in the house for good luck, and nobody sat on it. עולא says this is the דרגש the king reclines on during mourning.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
A bed of fortune.
phrases.notes: A special bed kept in the house for good luck that nobody actually sat on.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא עַרְסָא דְּגַדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A דרגש is an ערסא דגדא, a bed of fortune that was not sat on.

steps.title: The רבנן: why seat him now on a bed he never sat on?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask עולא how it makes sense to seat a mourner on a bed he was never allowed to sit on before.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to עולא: Is there anything that until now we did not let him sit on, and now, while he is mourning, we seat him on it?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge עולא's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bed of fortune was never used for sitting. The רבנן think it is strange that a mourner, who is supposed to sit lower and with less comfort, would suddenly be given a seat he never used before.

phrases.english: The Sages said to Ulla:
Is there anything
that until now we did not seat him on,
and now we seat him on it?
phrases.notes: 'Now' means during his time of mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְעוּלָּא מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's answer in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's definition of דרגש as ערסא דגדא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is unreasonable that a mourner would begin sitting on a bed that was never sat on before.

steps.title: רבא: it is just like being fed by others
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the רבנן's question: mourners also get fed by others now, which never happened before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects: What is the difficulty? Maybe it is just like eating and drinking. Until now we did not feed him or give him drink, and now we feed him and give him drink.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא says the רבנן's question is not a real problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During mourning, other people serve the mourner his meal, something they never did before. So it is not strange that mourning also brings a new kind of seat. Something new happening during mourning is not a reason to reject עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? (meaning: this is not a real question)

phrases.english: Rava objects to it:
What is the difficulty?
Perhaps it is just like eating and drinking,

phrases.aramaic: דְּעַד הָאִידָּנָא לָא אֹכְילִנֵּיהּ וְלָא אַשְׁקִינֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: that until now we did not feed him or give him drink,

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא קָא מוֹכְלִינַן לֵיהּ וְקָא מַשְׁקִינַן לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and now we feed him and give him drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא מַאי קוּשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the קשיא of step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the רבנן's question only, not the search for a better challenge.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Mourning already brings new treatment, like being fed by others, so a new seat is not strange.

steps.title: רבא's better question: why doesn't a דרגש get overturned?
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא saying a דרגש is stood up and not overturned, even though a mourner overturns every bed in his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty: a ברייתא says a דרגש does not need to be overturned; rather, he stands it up. If you think it is a bed of fortune, why doesn't it need to be overturned? Another ברייתא says that one who overturns his bed during mourning overturns not only his own bed but every bed in his house!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces the weak question with a stronger one against עולא, built on the mourning rule of overturning beds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mourner must overturn every bed in his house, not just his own. A bed of fortune is still a bed in the house, so it should be overturned too. Since the ברייתא says a דרגש is only stood up, a דרגש seems to be something other than a bed of fortune.

keyTerms.meaning: If there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty
To overturn it (a mourning practice for beds)
He stands it up on its side
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two ברייתות here. The first says a דרגש is only stood up. The second says every bed in the house gets overturned. The question comes from putting them side by side.

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty:
A dargash does not need to be overturned,
rather, he stands it up.
And if you think it is a bed of fortune,
why does it not need to be overturned?
But wasn't it taught:
One who overturns his bed,
does not overturn only his own bed,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כׇּל מִטּוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ הוּא כּוֹפֶה.
phrases.english: rather, he overturns all the beds he has in his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי קַשְׁיָא הָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting aside the רבנן's question, רבא offers a stronger challenge to עולא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's definition of דרגש as ערסא דגדא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every bed in the house must be overturned, so a bed of fortune should be too. Yet a דרגש is only stood up, so it can't be a bed of fortune.

steps.title: Pushback: maybe it is like a bed used for storage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a bed of fortune could be like a bed used for storing things, which also does not need to be overturned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Perhaps it is just like a bed set aside for storing things, as a ברייתא teaches: if it was set aside for storing things, he does not need to overturn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's challenge and defends עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every bed has to be overturned. A bed used only for storage is left alone. A bed of fortune isn't slept on either, so it could fit the same exception, and the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside, designated for one use
Things, belongings (here: items stored on the bed)

phrases.english: What is the difficulty?

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמִּטָּה מְיוּחֶדֶת לְכֵלִים,
phrases.english: Perhaps it is just like a bed set aside for storing things,
as it is taught:
If it was set aside for storing things,
he does not need to overturn it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קוּשְׁיָא דִּילְמָא מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמִּטָּה מְיוּחֶדֶת לְכֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קשיא of step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the overturning challenge. עולא's definition still stands for now.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule of overturning every bed already has an exception for beds not used for sleeping, and a bed of fortune can fit that exception.

steps.title: The real problem: a דרגש has straps
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a דרגש is handled by loosening its straps. A bed of fortune has no straps, so עולא's definition fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that with a דרגש, the mourner loosens the straps and it falls on its own. If you think it is a bed of fortune, does it have straps?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a final, stronger challenge that knocks out עולא's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל describes a דרגש as something held up by straps (קרביטין). Loosening them makes it collapse. A bed of fortune is not built with straps, so a דרגש must be a different kind of bed.

keyTerms.meaning: Straps that hold the bed together

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A dargash: he loosens the straps
and it falls on its own.
And if you think it is a bed of fortune,
does it have straps?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי קַשְׁיָא הָא קַשְׁיָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the overturning challenge was pushed back, the גמרא brings a stronger challenge from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's definition of דרגש as ערסא דגדא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A דרגש has straps that can be loosened, but a bed of fortune has none, so the two can't be the same thing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge is never answered. The גמרא drops עולא's definition and looks for a new one in the next step.

steps.title: רבין: a דרגש is a leather bed
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רב תחליפא, who knew the leather market, explained that a דרגש is a leather bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רבין came he said: One of the Sages told me, and his name was רב תחליפא, who often spent time in the leather workers' market, and he said to him: What is a דרגש? A leather bed.
steps.whatsHappening: Since עולא's definition fell, the גמרא brings a new definition from רבין: a דרגש is a leather bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב תחליפא spent time in the leather market, so he knew what this item was. A leather bed would be held up by leather straps, which fits רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's description of loosening the straps.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's 'bed of fortune' is rejected because a דרגש has straps. The accepted definition is רבין's: a leather bed (ערסא דצלא).

phrases.english: Rather, when Ravin came he said:
One of the Sages told me,
and Rav Tachlifa was his name,
who was often in the market of the leather workers,
and he said to him: What is a dargash?
A leather bed.
